summary: Iteration 119 regression. CRITICAL security fix on POST /api/user/reset-password VERIFIED — bogus/empty/missing tokens all rejected with HTTP 400 'Invalid or expired reset token' and login with real password still works. Legit forgot-password → verify-otp → reset-password flow works and session identity (not body email) is used; reused token rejected. OTP lockout after 5 wrong codes returns 'Too many incorrect attempts...' and Redis dedup key sec-alert:otp_lockout is present (alert path exercised; outbound email suppressed by DISABLE_OUTBOUND_EMAIL=true as expected). All 12 authenticated read endpoints return 200 with finite numeric amounts — no NaN/Infinity, no exponent-notation strings, valid JSON. Pre-migration snapshot parity holds on all endpoints whose data isn't live-DB-driven (payment-links, invoices, customers, referral, tickers, getAllTransactions); dashboard/dashboard-chart/recent-transactions/fee-tiers/wallet show minor drift explained entirely by new transactions arriving in the live DB (order shifted, tx count +1 to +2, monthly_volume delta ~$28) — not a rounding regression. Frontend Playwright (viewport 1920x1080) logged in and rendered /dashboard /transactions /wallet /invoices /payment-links /settings without NaN/undefined/exponent-notation/error-boundary. Amount formatting on /transactions confirmed: crypto shows up to 8 decimals with trailing zeros trimmed (e.g. '0.00037169 BTC', '0.00106489 BTC'), fiat shows 2 decimals ('$26.78', '$68.30', '$98.00').

minor.issue: Returns 500 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' when body omits currencyList — should validate input and 400 instead of 500.

Public {BASE}/health returns Next.js 404 (routed to frontend); only /api/* is proxied to backend. Backend /health works locally but is not reachable through public ingress. The API 404 JSON at /api/nope works correctly.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limiters share IP budgets across runs: /forgot-password and /reset-password use strictRateLimiter (20 per 15min per IP), /forgot-password/verify-otp uses otpRateLimiter (10 per 15min per IP+email). If a run has just been executed, expect 429s on the legit-reset path; the reset-password bypass tests themselves are 400-fast and NOT rate-limited (they short-circuit before the limiter counter in most cases — but the reset-password IP limiter DOES count them). To rerun cleanly wait 15 minutes or run only the bypass subclass in isolation. Redis dedup key for OTP-lockout alert: sec-alert:otp_lockout:<email>:json (TTL 1h) — presence means the alert was suppressed as designed, not that it failed. verify-otp response returns {data:{resetToken:...}}, not resetSessionToken. /api/wallet/getCurrencyRates body must include source, amount, currencyList[], fixedDecimal.
rca of the issue: N/A — the previously reported reset-password bypass (arbitrary email + bogus token could reset any account) is now blocked by hasOtpSession() in controller/user/passwordReset.ts:resetPassword. The session identity is read from Redis via the token and the request body email is deliberately ignored. Verified with 3 bypass payloads + a positive control (attacker email in body but valid session token still resets the real owner's password to the same value).
